Revenue has been rising (Sep-2025 quarter +9.0% YoY, Dec-2025 quarter +14.1%), while TTM operating margin is 9.0%. Management's Feb-2026 call says US customers accepted the tariff pass-through, but the amount is not quantified.
contradictions: TTM operating margin 9.0%, below the 10% line, while the order inflow is about 31% of TTM revenue; execution and margin on the new work are not yet known.
The Toyota programme was postponed (2025-02 call), and the packet has no customer-level confirmation of the Rs 720 crore inflow.
result.next_milestone: Disclosure of the customer split, execution schedule and value per programme for the Rs 720 crore inflow, and quarterly revenue growth above the FY25 run rate.

result.mechanism: The INR 5,000 crore order is for fuses placed with Bharat Electronics in December, per the transcript, and so is not a Rico order. The Hero item is a concluded price increase on specific components, with purchase orders received for those parts, and the packet gives no quantified uplift. result.rationale: The INR 5,000 crore 'FIRM' order is Bharat Electronics' fuse order, so the trigger belongs to another company and is a fatal flaw. The Hero price increase is a concluded pass-through on existing components with no quantified value, and it is ordinary cost recovery, not a change in trajectory. Revenue is falling and FY24 guidance was cut to about INR 2,300 crore, so the packet shows no operating inflection. Rejected.

No disqualifier applies: leverage is low and the customers are external OEMs; the open questions are margin and timing, which deep research should test.

The packet's 1,000 crore trigger is an annualised base of repriced and replaced business, not new revenue; the sizable new revenue is about Rs 363 crore a year of new business picked up from April 2020 (about 20% of trailing revenue of Rs 1,802 crore), which the company says is additional and mostly starts by mid or late 2022. The FCC Japan collaboration and 1986 commercial production are historical and not counted.

result.next_milestone: Ramp of the new programmes through mid and late 2022, and quarterly operating margin reaching management's first target of 12% to 12.5%

Management guidance of about Rs 2,000 cr turnover next year and margin target of 12-12.5% are guidance, not order-backed
result.next_milestone: Customer purchase orders or awards for wheels at the about Rs 300 cr a year run-rate, and commissioning of the expanded wheel plant
missing_information: No wheel customer, award or order volume quantified; the Rs 300 cr figure is not contracted
Wheel plant expansion capex and timing not specified beyond total FY22 capex of about Rs 80-90 cr (mainly Toyota-related)
Routine order flow: new programme wins of Rs 363 cr a year and Rs 6,250 cr over 2018-2020 indicate a regular win rate, so the non-wheel programmes are business as usual
TTM PAT is a loss of Rs 28.5 cr; balance sheet and debt structure not in packet beyond the call
Commodity cost pressure and premium freight effects on margins not quantified
Trigger event dates on the call (17 Feb 2021) differ from the packet filing date (24 Feb 2021)

reviews.rationale: Size: the stated wheel uplift from about Rs 50 cr to Rs 300 cr a year is about Rs 250 cr, or 19% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,317 cr, but it is management's expectation rather than contracted volume. Firmness: not firm, since no wheel award or order is cited and most of the Rs 1,000 cr headline is annualised programme value from 2018-2020 wins with starts still to come. The wheel step-up after import curbs is non-routine, but the broader order flow is routine (about Rs 6,250 cr of programme wins over 2018-2020, per the call), so it is not an inflection on its own. Watch for customer awards that convert the wheel uplift into firm orders; no disqualifier identified, though funding and loss-making TTM are unresolved.

events.quote: We have seen multiple changes, not only on the top line growth side, but on the margin guidance and on this 3x top line growth that you're talking about by 2030, then board level changes, then a lot of process optimization and back-to-back SAP implementation, then talking to customers for price increases.
So now you guided that why it took us almost 5 years where we did a capex of INR1,000 crores, where we could not be able to grow the top line, even the onetime of capex that we did.

Besides this, the price increases that because of the inflation of the rupee getting weak, all the other imports, the prices have gone up, and we have also taken up that with our overseas as well as the domestic customers, which is under negotiation at the moment.

Looking ahead, the cessation of temporary air freight, progressive realization of customer price revisions and cost pass-throughs, together with the benefit from our ongoing efficiency initiatives are expected to support a progressive improvement in the profitability from Q3 onwards.
We continue to engage actively with our customers for appropriate price revisions and cost pass-throughs.
We remain confident to exit the current year near to our targeted full year margins through customer price revisions and continued improvement in operating efficiency.
And in that period, we have done a capex of almost INR1,000 crores on an average of INR200 crores per year.
So there are almost about 40 launches which are taking place at the moment and all new products, and you'll see the impact coming up in the coming quarters.
The company has also secured new orders worth approximately INR2,500 crores over a program life of 5 years, providing strong visibility for future growth.
And we are already -- we, I think, in about a month's time, once we get all the clarification, we should be , we will be approaching our customers for a price revision there also.

Arvind Kapur: See, on the tariff front, whatever reduction has been given, but firstly, I must appreciate our customers, all the customers in the U.S. we requested them for the total price increase, the total tariff to be transferred to us, they all accepted, they all agreed.
And lately, when he introduced the new tariff for commercial vehicles, on that, he's -- from 10%, he's taken it up to 50% on commercial vehicles.
And if you are linking ourselves to growth or launch of some new products coming, then we are linking our numbers with some outcomes at the consumption end.
